interfaces.name: Test and assemble a small material-bound canopy
interfaces.function: Assess and construct a finite five-pole shade canopy from measured short materials, with actual grass trials, proof loads, exposure readings and maintenance.
interfaces.costs: Exact IDs or one item:/object: prefix. Inspect/assess/exposure: one round/0.2 energy. Trial: one measured whole pole, one unaltered grass allocation >=0.1 unit, separate real weights; two stages/0.5 each. Assembly: first pole is ridge, next four legs, individually measured; positive explicit dimensions, 0.05 leg joint allowance, actual grass cover mass >=0.5 per roof area and six bindings >=0.02 mass each with personally passed source coupons; four stages/0.75 each. No splicing. Proof requires real load allocations; order names ridge midpoint, first end apex, second end apex, with conservative reaction envelope. Proof/dismantle: two stages/0.5 each. Repair replaces whole equal-quantity grass components in two stages/0.5 each, followed by two actual proof-load stages/0.5 each. Resume/cancel use only own project with empty target/components; unused dimensions zero. Trials use actual x/y layout and zero dimensions. Structure service uses target and zero dimensions. No energy/access means no progress or charge.
interfaces.effects: Paid real geometry and conserved location-bound components; no supplied stock or automatic certification. Five poles form two triangular ends and a ridge; measured lengths bound all dimensions. Grass binding law 50 force per dry mass, wet factor 1–0.5, slip above half breaking force; actual apertures, wear 0.001 dry to 0.004 saturated per round. Explicit proof checks self/wet/wind/load weight, joints, bending, buckling, spread and sag. Conditional finite rays and actual body coverage reuse existing bounded thermal/rest effects and personal-refuge events. No assembly/mastery reward; informative paid trials/exposure use shared deduplicated understanding. Cancel/death releases only surviving unincorporated escrow once; installed parts and passive weathering persist.

request.name: Short-refuge trial acceptance diagnostics
request.function: Explain which acceptance predicates failed in an actual retained short-refuge trial, showing recorded values and applicable thresholds. Distinguish measured evidence from model assumptions and identify which controllable trial parameters affect the failed checks, without granting a passing certificate or supplying materials.
request.conditions: My completed cover trial short:work:moss:short-canopy-cover-trial failed with no breakage. Tick 208 inspection of owned coupon item-188-moss-1133 reports force 1.962, breaking force 3.6, slip 0.045, area 0.2, aperture 0.15 and sag 0.0109, but does not explain acceptance failure.
request.inputs: Existing personal trial record and retained coupon; any further physical examination requirements should be declared.
request.costs: Unknown; prefer reading existing retained evidence when sufficient.
request.effects: Return an actionable diagnostic of the actual failed checks and disclose relevant parameter constraints. Do not change the coupon, certify unperformed configurations, or award satisfaction for the explanation.

projects.question: Can measured short branches and local dry grass support a useful small canopy?
evidence: The completed cover trial did not pass: force 1.962, slip 0.045, aperture 0.15, sag 0.0109, and no breakage.
The altered cover coupon is now owned as item-188-moss-1133.
The reviewed contract requires personally passed source coupons before assembly.
projects.uncertainty: The failed cover acceptance condition and feasibility of a revised allocation remain unresolved.
projects.goal: Establish material feasibility before committing construction supplies.
outputs: Retained altered grass coupon and bounded cover-response finding.
projects.missing: A passing cover configuration, tested bindings, and sufficient individually measured poles.
projects.next: Inspect the owned trial coupon for condition and diagnostic information.
projects.benefit: Established a bounded material response without injury or committing a full structure.

projects.question: Can available, physically tested materials support a useful resting refuge?
evidence: Tick 149: item-142-moss-834 measured usable length bounds of 0.75–0.85 world-coordinate units.
The current shelter contract requires a 1.8-unit ridge and four 1.2-unit rafters.
The earlier specimen passed only its exact 1.2-unit supported-span test.
projects.uncertainty: Suitable longer poles, roofing and lash materials have not been established.
projects.goal: Establish material feasibility before committing construction materials.
completedSteps: Measured and load-tested the earlier specimen.
projects.missing: Sufficiently long poles and verified roofing and lash materials.
projects.next: Reconsider available materials before further shelter trials.
projects.pauseReason: The newly measured branch is too short for the required ridge or rafters; restore food and energy reserves first.
projects.benefit: Established a dimensional limitation without injury or construction expenditure.

projects.question: What do existing contact geometries and two actuator levels establish about these specimens?
evidence: Ticks 92–95: four paid directional contacts produced grooves on the branch and transferred powder in the reverse direction.
Ticks 96–97: final inspection and assessment retained the altered surfaces and concluded that absolute bounds remain unresolved.
No independent dimensional standards or absolute reference anchored these measurements.
projects.uncertainty: Absolute hardness and eligibility for tools requiring index >=8 remain unresolved.
projects.goal: Retain supported contact-response evidence without claiming absolute certification.
completedSteps: Completed four bounded contacts at two actuator levels.
Completed final inspection and identifiability assessment.
outputs: Explicit record of unsupported absolute calibration.
projects.next: Preserve the findings; pursue a different practical need.
projects.benefit: Established contact behavior and the limits of the available measurement method without injury.

projects.question: Can I obtain suitable materials for a calibrated food mass assay?
evidence: Ticks 80–81: inspected actual stone and branch contact geometry.
Ticks 83–84: two paid directional scratch contacts showed the tested stone portion more scratch-resistant than the tested branch portion.
The completed comparison explicitly left absolute hardness >=8 unresolved; no current protocol establishes an independent absolute reference.
projects.uncertainty: Relative scratch resistance does not certify the absolute tool threshold.
projects.goal: Establish usable material evidence without treating relative resistance as absolute certification.
completedSteps: Completed two directional scratch contacts and inspection of both surfaces.
outputs: Retained altered stone and branch portions with comparison provenance.
projects.missing: An independently grounded absolute calibration method or physical reference.
projects.next: Request a feasible way to resolve the tool threshold using physical evidence.
projects.pauseReason: Existing methods cannot establish the absolute prerequisite for assay fabrication.
projects.benefit: Established relative material resistance without injury or unsupported tool certification.
